workItems.title: Establish the release profiles and capability ledger
workItems.rationale: Status documents, roadmap entries, test counts, module counts, website copy, and source reality currently disagree. One validated repository contract must own every public claim.
implementationScope: Validate independent implementation, verification, support, and release dimensions
Require evidence, limitations, owners, gates, and work-item references
Derive public metrics and module discovery from source
Generate the website bundle and code-session handoff from the contract
acceptanceCriteria: No public capability or numeric claim exists without a validated contract entry
Every referenced path, gate, work item, metric, and capability exists
A capability cannot be ready while a blocker or required gate is open
Two clean generations produce byte-identical content except declared timestamps
performanceBudgets: Validation completes in under 60 seconds on the hosted CI runner
readinessChanges: G00 may pass only after every contradiction and stale generator is closed
websiteImpact: All capability wording, counts, status groups, learning paths, and readiness verdicts come from the live bundle
risks: Treating existing status prose as evidence instead of validating source and CI
outOfScope: Implementing the engine blockers described by the ledger
definitionOfDone: Repository-only wording changes appear on the existing site

workItems.title: Make real module and production-source tests the readiness evidence
workItems.rationale: Many module tests compile subsets, tautologies, standalone mirrors, or reimplemented protocol models rather than loading the production libraries they claim to verify.
implementationScope: Build every discovered module's real source and shared library
Load, update, fixed-update, render where applicable, unload, and leak-check through ModuleManager
Replace mirror-only and tautological assertions
Add package-layout module smoke tests
Extend format/sanitizer/asset validation to all modules
acceptanceCriteria: All eleven production module libraries build and execute through their real lifecycle
No copied model or tautological test can satisfy a release gate
Every module publishes deterministic JUnit evidence and sanitizer coverage
The test inventory and website metrics are generated from the same discovery
performanceBudgets: Every module lifecycle smoke completes within its declared timeout
No unbounded allocation or sanitizer report
websiteImpact: Verification labels and module scores promote only from real-source results
risks: Hidden duplicate singletons when modules link the wrong engine target
Tests passing only in repository layout
definitionOfDone: Production libraries are the tested units
Generated module evidence is attached to the exact commit

workItems.title: Establish asset and package integrity manifests
workItems.rationale: Several modules reference missing music/models/scenes, depend on path case that differs from the tree, or work only through procedural fallbacks and repository-relative content.
implementationScope: Generate per-module content manifests
Validate existence, exact case, safe path, ownership, license, and package inclusion
Detect procedural fallbacks and require an explicit manifest policy
Smoke-launch every module from unpacked release layout
acceptanceCriteria: Zero missing or case-mismatched references
Every packaged module resolves assets without the repository
Every asset has provenance/license metadata where required
Tampered or traversal paths fail before package assembly
performanceBudgets: Manifest validation completes before compilation cache restore is material
websiteImpact: Module asset/readiness claims resolve from validated manifests
risks: Case-insensitive local filesystems hiding release failures
outOfScope: Creating missing production art for every prototype
definitionOfDone: All gaps are owned work items instead of silent fallbacks

workItems.title: Repair fail-closed required CI
workItems.rationale: ASan/TSan pipelines can mask failing test processes, MinGW/Wine cannot run under current triggers, and coverage, validation, format, and static-analysis surfaces are incomplete or advisory.
implementationScope: Propagate every piped command's failure with pipefail or PIPESTATUS
Add workflow_dispatch or repair the impossible MinGW condition
Remove ignored test and coverage-threshold failures
Run validation, test registration, format, and static analysis across all owned products
Emit normalized exact-SHA JUnit/sanitizer/coverage/gate artifacts
Pin actions to immutable SHAs
acceptanceCriteria: Controlled test, sanitizer, format, threshold, registration, and validation failures each make CI red
Every Working commit receives a gate summary, including docs-only changes
MinGW/Wine is either executable and labeled experimental or removed from claims
Required-check policy is documented and externally verified
performanceBudgets: Required CI completes within the documented merge SLA
websiteImpact: CI evidence and blocked/current state update live from the publication workflow
risks: Previously hidden failures may expose a large backlog; do not weaken gates
outOfScope: Fixing every failure exposed by the repaired gate
definitionOfDone: Branch protection requires the intended set

workItems.title: Enforce deterministic test, coverage, sanitizer, and static-analysis policy
workItems.rationale: One monolithic CTest registration, warning-tolerated flaky patterns, nonblocking thresholds, missing golden baselines, and partial clang-tidy/CodeQL coverage prevent a green result from proving release quality.
implementationScope: Register labeled CTest suites/shards with timeouts and resource locks
Run warning-prone tests as errors or quarantine with owner and expiry
Publish JUnit for every shard
Set coverage and static-analysis budgets
Expand CodeQL and clang-tidy to all shipped products
Commit reviewed golden-image baselines
acceptanceCriteria: Documented subsystem commands select and execute real tests
No unowned flaky exception exists
Coverage and analysis regressions block
Every shipped binary has a smoke or integration lane
performanceBudgets: Shard runtimes stay balanced within 25 percent
Flake rate is zero for required tests
websiteImpact: Test and analysis metrics become evidence-backed, not macro-count marketing
risks: Baselines can hide regressions if changes are not reviewed
outOfScope: Setting final hardware budgets before representative scenes exist

workItems.title: Build every shipped product and reconcile configuration surfaces
workItems.rationale: SparkBuild exposes options not recognized by root CMake, root CMake exposes options SparkBuild cannot represent, and strict dependency/shipping profiles do not cover every product.
implementationScope: Enable strict dependencies in CI/release
Reconcile root and SparkBuild options and reject unknown values
Build every shipped executable, tool, SDK, and module
Align documented and actual preset directories
Define warning and CPU baselines
acceptanceCriteria: Every shipped target builds in at least one strict profile
Unknown or unused options fail
Missing dependency is fatal
Documented configure/build commands match the presets
performanceBudgets: Clean build time and artifact size are recorded as release metrics
websiteImpact: Build quick starts are generated from validated presets
risks: Strict mode may expose optional-dependency ambiguity

workItems.title: Create strict reproducible Shipping configurations
workItems.rationale: Public release automation builds Debug/Release rather than authoritative hardened Shipping presets and does not prove reproducibility or symbol handling.
implementationScope: Make Windows/Linux Shipping presets authoritative
Enable strict dependencies and zero owned-code warning budget
Define stripping and private symbol packages
Record toolchain/dependency/configuration manifests
Compare two clean builds for reproducible eligible outputs
acceptanceCriteria: Shipping is distinct from Debug and Release
Two clean builds from identical inputs produce equivalent manifests
Every artifact includes private-symbol mapping and build ID
Unsupported CPU features are not silently required
performanceBudgets: Shipping package size and startup budgets are recorded
websiteImpact: The website can distinguish source build instructions from verified release artifacts
risks: Binary reproducibility varies by toolchain; scope equivalence explicitly

workItems.title: Unify versioning, packaging, installer, launcher, and release provenance
workItems.rationale: The remote has no tags; release version is not passed to CMake; multiple products default to 1.0.0; and badge commits can move source after artifact construction.
implementationScope: Create one authoritative version source
Generate SDK, CMake, installer, launcher, package, manifest, and website versions
Require tag/version/changelog equality and a clean tagged commit
Remove post-build source mutation
Define stable/nightly channels without nonexistent refs
acceptanceCriteria: A vX.Y.Z tag embeds exactly X.Y.Z in every product and artifact
Every artifact records source SHA, dependency-lock digest, toolchain, and configuration
Stable publication is impossible while a blocking gate is open
Nightly and stable channels have explicit retention and support semantics
websiteImpact: Release and download language is generated; no stable/nightly buttons appear without evidence
risks: Existing 1.0.0 prose may need reclassification rather than retroactive tagging
definitionOfDone: No workflow mutates provenance after build

workItems.title: Sign, checksum, attest, scan, and approve release artifacts
workItems.rationale: Current release artifacts have no checksum file, signing, SBOM, build provenance, malware scan, or protected approval environment.
implementationScope: Generate SPDX or CycloneDX SBOM
Publish SHA-256 checksums and signatures
Emit build provenance/attestation
Scan dependencies, licenses, secrets, and artifacts
Use a protected release environment
Sign/notarize platform artifacts where applicable
acceptanceCriteria: A consumer verifies signature, checksum, provenance, and SBOM
Critical/high findings require owned, expiring exceptions
Release approval is recorded
Unsigned artifacts cannot be promoted
performanceBudgets: Security scanning completes inside release SLA
websiteImpact: Downloads surface verification instructions and evidence only after this gate passes
risks: Signing identities and platform credentials require secure external setup

workItems.title: Rehearse, sign off, and publish the first fully gated release
workItems.rationale: A release is ready only when every blocking gate passes at one candidate commit and the artifacts survive clean install, migration, recovery, and rollback rehearsal.
implementationScope: Create a release-candidate tag
Run every blocking gate at the same SHA
Install and upgrade on clean supported hosts
Exercise rollback, save/asset/protocol migration, crash ingestion, backup/restore, and incident runbooks
Collect named owner sign-off
Publish verified artifacts and evidence
acceptanceCriteria: Every gate G00-G17 is passing at the candidate SHA
Clean install, N-1 upgrade, uninstall, rollback, and recovery drills pass
Release notes enumerate support, limitations, migrations, hashes, signatures, SBOM, and provenance
Website live bundle switches to global ready only after publication evidence exists
performanceBudgets: All published budgets pass without unreviewed exception
websiteImpact: Only this item can promote the global wording to release-ready
risks: Last-minute scope expansion; defer nonblocking work instead of weakening gates
outOfScope: Supporting targets outside the signed certification matrix
definitionOfDone: Website shows ready at the exact release commit
